goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3 uses `embed: :ids` without `include: true`, so embeddable host objects aren't sideloaded and the client hydration produces an array of undefined, rendering empty admin table rows

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201 unconditionally runs `delete obj[k]` in the plural branch (unlike the singular branch), destroying raw ids and replacing them with undefined whenever a collection isn't sideloaded — a global regression for every model

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `_hydrateEmbedded` to handle keys ending in `_ids` via a new plural branch. In that branch it does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` and then *always* assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` and *always* `delete obj[k]`. Unlike the singular `_id` branch, there is no check that `_lookupSubType` actually found anything before deleting the raw ids. If the related records are not present in `root` (not sideloaded), `_lookupSubType(...)` will return `undefined`/`null`, producing an array of undefineds while also deleting the original `*_ids` array. This is a correctness regression visible in the diff (and additionally can throw if `obj[k]` is not an array).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:197 calls `obj[k].map(...)` without guarding against a null or non-array `*_ids` value, which throws; the `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` the new plural branch for keys matching `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` does `obj[k].map(...)` when `m[2]` is truthy (i.e., for `*_ids`). There is no guard that `obj[k]` is an Array; if the server returns `null`, `undefined`, or a non-array for a `*_ids` field, this will throw (`Cannot read property 'map' of null/undefined`). Also, `hydrated || []` is effectively useless for this case because execution never reaches it if `map` throws, and when `map` succeeds it always returns an array (truthy), so the `|| []` fallback won't be used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 uses `create_table ... force: true`, which silently drops and recreates a pre-existing table, destroying data instead of failing loudly

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` contains `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table first if it already exists and then recreate it, which would destroy any existing `embeddable_hosts` data instead of raising an error. This behavior is directly implied by the option used in the diff, so the risk described is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration create_embeddable_hosts.rb:26 string-interpolates host values into raw SQL without quoting, so a host containing a single quote breaks the migration mid-run; should use connection.quote or bind params

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration loops through `records.each do |h|` and runs:

```rb
execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
```

`h` is interpolated directly into a SQL string inside single quotes without any escaping/quoting helper. If `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL-significant characters), the generated SQL becomes invalid and can break the migration mid-run; it also creates a SQL injection risk from the `site_settings` value. Using `connection.quote(h)` or parameterized/bound execution would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No uniqueness validation on EmbeddableHost#host and no unique index in the migration, allowing duplicate rows for the same domain so record_for_host arbitrarily picks one, affecting the destination category for imported topics

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbeddableHost` with only a format validation on `host` and no `validates_uniqueness_of` (or equivalent) on `host`. The migration `create_embeddable_hosts` also creates no unique index on `host` (or `lower(host)`), so the DB will allow duplicates. Lookup uses `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` -> `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, which will return an arbitrary matching row if duplicates exist. That return value is then used in `TopicEmbed.import` to choose the category (`eh.try(:category_id)`), so duplicates can cause inconsistent/incorrect category selection for imported embeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1404 test "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests embeddable host behavior since expandable_first_post? dropped that condition; it passes for unrelated reasons and its name documents nonexistent behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from requiring `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` to no longer checking embeddable hosts at all (`SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). That means any existing spec case named/claiming behavior like “is false if embeddable_host is blank” is no longer actually testing a condition that affects the method, and could now pass/fail based only on `embed_truncate`/`has_topic_embed?` defaults rather than embeddable host configuration. This makes the test misleading/invalid relative to the updated implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 uses `type.replace('_', '-')` which only replaces the first underscore, so model names with two underscores won't resolve to the /admin/ base path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `basePath(store, type)` to check `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-')) !== -1`. While it’s true JS `String#replace` only replaces the first underscore, the only admin model added/used here is `embeddable-host` (corresponding to `embeddable_host`, which has a single underscore). The other entries (`plugin`, `site-customization`) also do not require multiple underscore replacements. The finding describes a hypothetical edge case (types with 2+ underscores), but the diff provides no evidence such a model/type exists or is impacted here, so it’s not a verifiable problem introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 runs `lower(host) = ?` on an unindexed column for every embed request and TopicRetriever call; there's no index on host and the lower() wrapper would defeat a plain index

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` which queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). The migration creating `embeddable_hosts` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) does not add any index on `host`, so this lookup will require a scan of the table. Additionally, because the query wraps the column in `lower(host)`, even adding a plain index on `host` would not be used by many DBs without a functional index. This lookup is invoked on embed requests (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` now calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`) and in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, so it is on hot paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:47 calls destroyRecord() without `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, so a failed delete leaves the row in place with no admin feedback

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` but does not attach a `.catch(popupAjaxError)` (unlike `save()`, which explicitly does). If the server delete fails (network error/validation/500), the promise rejection is unhandled and no admin-facing error is shown. Also, since `deleteHost` is only sent inside the `then`, the row will remain, but without feedback about why deletion failed—matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 anchors the host format validation with `\Z`, which allows a trailing newline ("example.com\n") to pass validation and be stored despite never matching a lookup

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the validation regex is anchored with \A...\Z. In Ruby, \Z matches either the true end of string or just before a final trailing newline, so a value like "example.com\n" can pass validates_format_of. The before_validation block strips scheme and path but does not strip whitespace/newlines. Later, record_for_host(host) parses a URL and compares uri.host (which won’t include the newline) via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, so a stored host with a trailing newline would not match lookups/authorization checks. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the current validation anchor choice.
